title: Automatic publication maps that explain their choices — geo_automap
text: geo_automap() draws finished map one call, spirit GeoSpaX's AutoMap. looks data chooses, reason choice: projection: Equal Earth world-wide data (true areas), Lambert azimuthal equal-area projection centred data continents large regions, local UTM zone study areas (distances metres); symbology, following conventions GeoSpaX's AutoMap, ArcGIS QGIS: numbers points, lines polygons get graduated colours classes (classed legend, never continuous ramp). method follows shape data: equal intervals roughly symmetric (|skew| < 0.5), natural breaks (Jenks) skewed, quantiles heavy-tailed (|skew| >= 2); 5 classes 30 features, fewer small samples; colour ramp follows field's meaning: blues water rain, greens vegetation, viridis elevation, slope predictions, diverging ramp values cross zero, yellow-orange-red otherwise; small whole-number counts points get proportional circles; categories get qualitative Okabe-Ito colours; features without value get single symbol; continuous surfaces (raster x, background DEM sites) get stretched colour ramp gradient legend, place gradient legend used; basemap: none world regional maps background surface; topographic tiles study areas, muted context legend (coastline offline); furniture: graticule world outline world maps; scale bar north arrow regional local maps, corners chosen avoid data. Everything can overridden arguments, result normal ggplot can keep editing. geo_automap_explain() returns decisions table, ready methods section.

text: geo_breaks() returns class breaks numeric vector, geo_classify() adds class every row data frame, ready choropleth bubble map. styles follow tmap classInt: "quantile": equal numbers observations per class; "equal": equal-width classes range; "jenks": Fisher-Jenks natural breaks, minimise within-class sum squares exactly (Fisher 1958; computed C++). breaks equal classInt's "jenks" style; classInt's "fisher" style gives classes breaks halfway neighbouring values; "pretty": rounded breaks base::pretty(); "sd": breaks mean plus minus whole standard deviations; "fixed": breaks give. text: sdm_ensemble() fits several algorithms presence-background (presence-absence) data, scores spatial block cross-validation, combines one weighted ensemble, spirit biomod2 (Thuiller et al. 2009) without dependencies fixes common weaknesses: Spatial cross-validation default. Random folds put test points next training points, spatially autocorrelated data look better (Roberts et al. 2017). Folds whole spatial blocks. Comparable algorithms. Presence-background data fitted equal total weight presences background (Barbet-Massin et al. 2012) GLM GAM, Maxent uses infinitely-weighted formulation, random forest grows tree balanced bootstrap (-sampling; Valavi et al. 2021), four answer question 0-1 scale. Weights transferable skill. algorithm weighted cross-validated true skill statistic min_tss; algorithms left rather allowed dilute ensemble. Standardised predictors. Every algorithm sees predictors rescaled 0-1 training range, results depend units zero lies. Agreement uncertainty. Predictions give weighted mean weighted standard deviation across algorithms. random forest Maxent written C++ run several cores.
